Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the MedTech Innovations Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Dr. Emily Chen, Chief Technology Officer; and Michael Torres, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. MedTech Innovations achieved record results this third quarter, reflecting the strength of our diversified portfolio and our commitment to innovation.

Today, I will cover eight key aspects of our performance:
1. Gross margin trends and supply chain commentary
2. Competitive dynamics and market share trends
3. Inventory management and working capital optimization
4. SG&A expense management and efficiency gains
5. Key assumptions underlying the guidance
6. New product launches and contribution to growth
7. Hospital and ambulatory surgery center adoption rates
8. Strategic priorities and focus areas for the next quarter

Jordan will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. Dr. Chen will update us on our technology advancements, and Michael will discuss our market strategies. We'll then conclude with a Q&A session.

To start, let me highlight new product launches and their contribution to growth, a cornerstone of our success. As we close out a stellar quarter with total revenue of $2.8 billion, up 18% year-over-year on a constant currency basis, our innovations were pivotal. They represented 28% of overall revenue, totaling $785 million—a 52% jump from last year—and drove 65% of our incremental growth. Absent these, core growth would have been a respectable 6%, but they propelled us to high-teens expansion.

Leading the charge is our VitaFlex Pro robotic-assisted navigation system for spinal procedures, cleared by FDA PMA in Q1 and CE Mark soon after. It features AI-driven real-time imaging fusion and haptic feedback, cutting fluoroscopy exposure by up to 40% and speeding complex lumbar fusions by 25% in early user reports. In Q3, it posted $210 million in sales at an ASP of $1.2 million per unit, with recurring instrument revenue at 35% of sales and 78% gross margins. We've installed 450 bases worldwide, gaining ground on Globus Medical and SeaSpine with 60% quarter-over-quarter procedure growth.

In electrophysiology, the CardioPulse AI-enabled ablation catheter for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation generated $145 million, surpassing our $120 million target after 510(k) clearance. Its lattice-tip design and machine learning for lesion mapping achieved 95% first-pass pulmonary vein isolation in trials, outshining aspects of Johnson & Johnson's Biosense Webster offerings. U.S. hospital contracts ramped 30%, with 76% gross margins from U.S.-based laser etching efficiencies.

Our InsuLink 3.0 smart patch pump in diabetes care added $180 million, up 70% year-over-year, thanks to CGM connectivity and predictive algorithms matching Dexcom G7 standards, aiding A1c reductions prized by payers. Formulary wins with UnitedHealthcare and CVS Aetna, plus UK NHS tenders, boosted it, with 82% margins from Singapore localization covering 70% of components.

U.S. new product revenue was 62%, surging 55% on Medicare's CY2024 OPPS NTAP for VitaFlex Pro, ahead of Boston Scientific's EP segment. Europe at 22% gained traction in Germany and France post-MDR, with CardioPulse at 15% share in key accounts. Asia-Pacific soared 80% to $110 million on China NMPA for InsuLink and a Mindray JV for VitaFlex, tapping a $15 billion spinal market growing 15%. Emerging markets like Brazil and India rose 40% via distributors with lower-ASP variants.

This reflects our $1.2 billion R&D—18% of revenue—focused on precision navigation (40%), AI therapies (30%), and wearables (30%). Recent IDE filings include a bioresorbable-frame TAVR challenging Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien and a closed-loop SCS for pain akin to Nevro's HF10. Partnerships with NVIDIA for edge AI imaging and 3D Systems for implants accelerate us. Expect new products to fuel 55-60% of FY24 growth, with Q4 at $850 million midpoint, 150bps margin gains, and 2-3% share increases amid GPO pressures. Our 25 new patents this quarter fortify our moat for 12-15% organic growth outpacing Intuitive Surgical or Stryker.

Shifting to our strategic priorities and focus areas for next quarter, as we build on 14% revenue growth to $2.8 billion—powered by 22% EP procedural gains and double-digits in Structural Heart—our aims are mid-teens organic growth, EBITDA margins nearing 32%, and pipeline progress in cardiology, neuromodulation, and robotics surgery.

First, ramp commercial execution on launches and share. In Structural Heart, EvoFlex Ultra TAVR—mirroring Edwards' Sapien 3 Ultra strengths—holds 18% U.S. share post-August PMA, targeting 12,000 Q4 cases (35% sequential rise) at $32,000 ASPs buoyed by 2025 OPPS's 4.2% TAVR payment hike. We'll prioritize Southeast/Midwest high-volume sites with 28% imaging attach. EP's PulseMap AI catheter beats CARTO 3 benchmarks with 15% faster mapping and 92% first-pass success; 120 new U.S. reps aim for 500bps AFib share to 22%. Europe CE renewals and Japan PMDA push target JPY 5 billion.

Second, advance R&D with 12.5% revenue spend. NeuroStim Pro DBS trial data mid-quarter eyes 85% Parkinson's responder rates for Q1 2025 FDA, tapping $1.2 billion TAM. RoboSurge X robotics enters limited release with haptic feedback and 20% faster docking, training 250 surgeons at 50 sites for 15% soft-tissue penetration. MedConnect cloud platform aggregates 1.5 million cases for readmission analytics, aiding bundled payments now 28% of U.S. revenue.

Third, regional strategies: U.S. (72% revenue) leverages Boomer-driven 7% procedures and ASC shifts for 18% higher margins, moving 15% TAVR/EP outpatient. Europe (15%) grows 11% on MDR-certified items, German DRG for PulseMap, NHS TAVR. APAC/emerging (13%) at 25% YoY gets $50 million for Singapore hub, 30% of $4 billion robotics TAM; India Apollo tie for 5,000 Triad knee cases.

Fourth, operational excellence: Dual-source 95% components for 200bps gross margin to 68%; SG&A at 24% enables $500 million buybacks, 10% dividend rise. Sustainability cuts Scope 1/2 emissions 25% for EU CSRD.

This sets Q4 at $2.95-$3.05 billion (12-15% organic), EPS $1.85-$1.95. Risks: FX (3%), U.S. election reimbursement shifts, J&J competition. $28 billion backlog, 4.2x leverage support M&A.

I will now turn the call over to Jordan for a review of our financial results, where he'll delve into gross margins, competitive dynamics, inventory, SG&A, guidance assumptions, and adoption rates.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex outlined, we delivered exceptional financial performance this quarter, underscoring operational resilience in a dynamic medtech environment.

Let me begin with gross margin trends and supply chain dynamics, highlighting our portfolio strength and operational fortitude at MedTech Innovations. In Q3 FY24, GAAP gross margin reached 68.7%, expanding 250 basis points year-over-year from 66.2% and 110 basis points sequentially from Q2's 67.6%. Non-GAAP, stripping amortization from the CardioFlow Dynamics acquisition—their transcatheter heart valve tech—hit 69.4%, our best in over two years. This is the third straight sequential gain, aligning with full-year non-GAAP guidance of 68.5%-69.5%.

Drivers: Product mix added 160bps, led by Structural Heart (28% YoY growth) and Robotics (42%). High-margin EvoHeart TAVR (15,000+ global implants) and da Vinci Xi+ shifted away from 5% lower-margin legacy catheters. U.S. orthopedics ASPs rose 2%, countering CMS FY24 IPPS's 1.5% DRG trim for joints.

COGS improved 90bps despite inflation: PEEK/PLLA polymers up 8%, titanium for spinals up 12% from sanctions, freight +20bps on Red Sea issues. Offset by MedTech Manufacturing Excellence's $45 million quarterly savings (120bps), via neuromodulation chip yields to 98.2% and Galway catheter automation.

Supply chain: Post-2022 semiconductor woes costing industry $120 million (e.g., Abbott Infinity DBS, our NeuroStim leads), 85% critical components dual-sourced, 40% North America/Europe-localized. Austin, Texas greenfield at 50% for RF ablation generators cuts lead times to 8 weeks, dodging Mexico tariffs.

Regionally: U.S. (52% revenue) margins to 71.2% (+300bps) on VizIR imaging amid Stryker Mako-like capex. Europe (28%) to 66.8% (+100bps), 92% MDR-certified ahead of Boston Scientific. China (margins -150bps to 62.4%) volumes +35% on AccuStent, Suzhou localization for 20% savings.

For 72% by FY26: Carbon fiber hip implants (-18% costs like Zimmer ROSA), AI-ERP (95% disruption accuracy, inventory -22% to $450 million), $300 million nearshoring (30% electronics to Mexico/India), value-based high-acuity focus (95% instrument attach like Intuitive).

Q4: 69.5%-70.5%, mix/costs beat FX; rare earth risks green-rated.

Now, competitive dynamics and market share trends. The $538 billion global med devices market grows 5.4% CAGR to 2030 on demographics, volumes, value care; our $45 billion TAM at 7-9% on transcatheter/robotics.

Headline: +210bps global share to 14.2% in structural heart Q3, third straight quarter outpacing 8.2% segment growth. U.S. TAVR to 28.5% (+240bps), #2 behind Edwards' Sapien 32.7% (gap narrowed 420 to 185bps). Europe Medtronic Evolut FX took 1.1pts with 12.5% pacemaker rates vs. 15.2% avg; Boston LOTUS Edge 9.8%; niche JenaValve/Transept <3%.

Our ApexFlex TAVR's repositionability, 95% first-pass, APEX-3 trial's 18.4% 2-year mortality (beats Evolut 21.2%) drove 14% YoY U.S. high-volume share to 31.2%, ASP $32,500 (+2%). U.S. (62% rev) +12% procedures to 105,000 on hospital-at-home kits (-22% LOS). Europe (25%) +150bps to 12.8% on 24Fr compatibility. APAC (18%) +320bps to 8.4% via Japan/China partnerships, Singapore mfg vs. Terumo.

Tailwinds: TAVR cases 185,000 (+22%), reimbursement (UK NICE), supply resilience (dual nitinol, Minnesota mfg vs. Abbott resin issues). R&D 11.2% sales funds Pulsar neuromod (85% HTN response), Orion robotic AFib; $1.2B NeuroStim Dynamics adds 4% sacral share vs. Medtronic InterStim. Philips AI imaging +18% efficiency.

Expect 200-300bps more share to 16-17% by 2026; risks CMS transparency (-3-5% ASP), Edwards X4.

Next, inventory management and working capital optimization—critical for regulated products like stents, implants, stimulators amid volatility peers like Medtronic/Boston face (DIOs >110).

Q3 turns 4.2x (from 3.1x YoY), DIO 87 days (-25% YoY, -12 seq), CCC 45 days (from 68), freeing $142 million TTM for R&D/buybacks. WC/sales 14.2% vs. industry 18-20%.

Drivers: AI-SAP S/4HANA forecasting (-18% to 7% error on EmboShield), 95% service/15% less buffer. SKU cut 22% (legacy orthopedics like Stryker), VMI 35% off-balance (DPO 72 from 55). U.S. JIT Galway for orthos (-18 DIO), Europe RFID Leiden (<1% obsolescence), APAC Suzhou (-7 weeks to 75 DIO).

Tech: IBM blockchain 100% UDI/40% less holds, IoT DCs avert $8M spoilage; $25M CapEx 3.5x ROI, 2.2pts COGS save. Industry noble metals +15%, freight up; our hedging/multi-source (40% SE Asia, 30% Mexico) aids 210bps gross to 68.5%. Target 4.8x turns, <40 CCC by 2025 via Horizon 3.0 ML automation, Kaiser consignment.

This boosted FCF $285 million (+42% YoY).

On SG&A management and efficiency gains, vital amid CMS pressures, value care shift. Q3 SG&A $285 million, 24.8% revenue (-210bps YoY, -80 seq), fifth straight leverage; FY 25.2% (from 27.9%). YTD $52 million savings adjusted for 8% growth; core $60 million ex-$8M restructuring.

Selling (62%) $177 million (-7% YoY, 15.4%); G&A $108 million (-12%, 9.4%). SG&A Reset Initiative 70% to $150M FY25 target.

Field force: U.S. cardio reps 1,450 to 1,320, Veeva/Salesforce AI +18% efficiency, 112% quota (98% last), $134K/rep (-11%), 22 TAVR cases/rep (+14, CoreValve Evolut). Digital VR/HCP portals -25% demos, -$12M travel; Mako sales -20 days.

U.S. 23.5%, Medicare bundles; EMEA 26.2% Dublin SSC 40% indirect save; APAC 28.1% offset China VBP -15% ASP via Japan/India direct (-22% commissions). Emerging 8% from 11%.

G&A: SAP RPA 65% AP (-45 FTEs, 10 to 2 days), Coupa $18M consolidation; headcount -9% to 4,200, regulatory/digital focus for AI imaging 510(k)s.

Reinvest 20% savings ($10M/qtr) precision marketing (+16% structural volumes). Op margin +320bps to 28.4%; FY SG&A 25.0-25.5%, leverage to FY25 robotics/diagnostics.

Ahead: GenAI forecasting, Bangalore data center for resilience amid consolidation like Zimmer.

Turning to key assumptions underlying guidance—FY25 organic 9-11%, adj EPS $4.85-5.05, core gross 66-67% (+100-150bps). Grounded in procedural visibility, reimbursement, pipeline.

Procedures: U.S. 6-8% structural/EP/coronary (Vizient/Premier data), TAVR +12% Q3 but 7-9% slowdown offset Harmony TMVR (H1 FDA). EP 8-10% HPSD/PFA, Volt PF 15% U.S. share > Farapulse. EMEA 7-9% Watchman FLX +18%; APAC ex-China 10-12%, China 18-22% XiFlow +25% seq post-NRDL. Over-65 +3%/yr boosts CRM ICDs.

Pricing flat/+1%, U.S. +0.5% pass-through offset GPO/sequester; China -3-5% VBP. Mix +4% RhythmSync 20% attach.

Gross: 150bps Galway/Minnesota efficiencies (92-95% yields), 2-3% inflation derisked, Symetis TMVR +50bps mix -100bps launch.

OpEx: SG&A 32-33% +5% productivity Procedure360; R&D 12% $450M robotic PCI IDE Q2, NeuroFlex HTN; $1.2B CardioFlow synergies.

Macro: 50bps U.S. slowdown >4.5% rates, FX 1-2% (EUR1.08/Y150); LatAm 5%, India 15%+.

Tailwinds: 40% rev post-2022 launches >30% industry, 2-3pts share (15% lower mortality vs. MitraClip). Risks FDA/supply/Intuitive; stress 7% growth/$4.70 EPS.

Confident to beat 5-6% market.

Finally, hospital and ASC adoption rates, a leading indicator amid site-of-care shift per 2024 OPPS. Adoption (installs/active >50 procs/qtr PrecisionFlow Robotics/SmartNav) 28% of 5,200 U.S. hospitals/6,100 ASCs (+420bps YoY, 11th quarter up).

Hospitals: 42% Tier 1/2 (1,200 targets, +18% YoY) on PRECISION-H 32% complication/25% OR cuts vs. da Vinci Xi 55% share; our $1.6M capex lower.

ASCs: 16% (2,500 targets, +62% YoY >7% industry), volumes +145% on CMS 85% coverage vs. 72% HOPD; USPI 28 systems/22% gyn/urology.

Market: ASCs 14M cases +12%, robotics 15-20%/$4.5B TAM; hospitals consolidate to 78 carts/system (+ from 65). U.S. 82% installs; Europe 12% +35% SmartNav CE; APAC 24% Singapore/Korea to 40% FY25; China MicroPort 60%.

Pillars: PrecisionFlow Connect AI/EHR +18% throughput, VR training -12 procs ramp to 90 days; 150 VAC reps/112 approvals, 15% ASC rebates/40 deals; Medtronic neuromod, SCA 50 ASCs.

YE24 32-35%, $280-320M recurring 85% margins > Stryker Mako 14% ASC; $18B robotics TAM.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Chen for an update on our product pipeline.

Dr. Emily Chen:
Thank you, Jordan. We are excited about the progress we are making in our technology roadmap. Our latest innovation, the ApexFlex TAVR platform, is poised to transform structural heart interventions with superior repositionability and outcomes. We expect FDA approval in Q1 2025.

In R&D, we're advancing Pulsar neuromodulation in IDE trials showing 85% hypertension response, Orion robotic catheter for AFib challenging da Vinci in EP, and NeuroStim Pro DBS with adaptive AI. Manufacturing advances like Galway automation and Austin localization support scale. Clinical trials like APEX-3 confirm leadership, with six Phase III readouts in 2025. Our 11.2% R&D intensity fuels bioresorbables, AI imaging, and robotics, positioning us for TAM expansion.

Next, Michael with insights on our commercial strategy.

Michael Torres:
Thank you, Dr. Chen. We are focused on driving commercial excellence and expanding our global reach. Our strategic partnerships—like Philips AI integration, Mindray JVs, and IDN bundles with Kaiser/USPI—are enabling access to new markets and segments.

U.S. field optimization via Veeva AI boosts productivity; Europe MDR leadership accelerates approvals; APAC localization counters VBP/tariffs. Value-based models and ASC shifts drive attach rates >95% in high-acuity, mirroring razor-blade success. Surgeon training, VAC navigators, and digital tools shorten ramps, targeting share gains amid procedure booms.

Now, back to Alex for Q&A.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Michael. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions remain the same. Our first question comes from David Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Jordan, on the FY25 guidance, can you elaborate more on the procedural growth assumptions, especially with potential macro slowdowns?

Jordan Lee:
Sure, David. Our 6-8% U.S. procedural assumption draws from surgeon surveys, Vizient claims, aligning with Edwards/Medtronic TAVR +12% Q3 trends but prudently moderating to 7-9% as population matures, offset by TMVR/PFA acceleration—Volt PF already 15% share. Internationally, EMEA 7-9%, APAC ex-China 10-12%, China 18-22% post-NRDL. We've stress-tested for 50bps elective drag if rates >4.5%, still hitting 7% organic/$4.70 EPS. Aging demographics and backlog provide cushion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Great, thanks. Alex or Jordan, thoughts on supply chain risks persisting into Q4, given Red Sea and rare earths?

Jordan Lee:
Hi Lisa. We've built strong resiliency—85% dual-sourced criticals, 40% localized NA/EU, Austin ramping RF generators to 8-week leads. Rare earths for MRI/EP mitigated via SE Asia diversification; scorecard all green. Q4 gross 69.5-70.5% sees mix/cost tailwinds > modest FX. Multi-year efforts post-2022 shortages position us ahead of peers.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Raj Patel:
Thanks. Michael, on ASC adoption surging to 16%, how are you scaling commercial there, and any partnership updates?

Michael Torres:
Thanks, Raj. Explosive 62% YoY ASC growth leverages CMS 85% coverage, USPI 28 systems at 22% mix. Scaling via 15% rebate bundles closing 40 Q3 deals, VR training shortening ramps to 90 days, VAC team at 150 securing approvals. SCA Health for 50 more ASCs, Medtronic co-dev neuromod integration. YE24 32-35% adoption implies $300M recurring at 85% margins, outpacing Mako.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Rodriguez with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Rodriguez:
Congrats team. Dr. Chen, pipeline-wise, any updates on neuromod or robotics timelines amid competitive intensity?

Dr. Emily Chen:
Thanks, Emily. NeuroStim Pro DBS topline mid-Q4 targets 85% Parkinson's response for Q1 FDA, challenging Medtronic Percept in $1.2B TAM. RoboSurge X limited release with 250 trainings for 15% soft-tissue by YE, 20% faster docking. Synergies from NeuroStim Dynamics acquisition add sacral bolt-on. IDEs for robotic PCI, NeuroFlex HTN on track; 2025 Phase IIIs reinforce innovation edge.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your thoughtful questions. We remain confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver sustainable growth.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
